claim: Plain GPT-4-class LLMs write valid Blocksworld plans in only about a third of 600 instances (206/600 one-shot, 210/600 zero-shot); the same model class does worse on Logistics and near zero on disguised domains.
agent_test: Run our scaffold vs plain prompt on 100 Blocksworld and Logistics instances, valid-plan rate, equal tokens.

claim: Disguising the action names (Mystery Blocksworld) collapses GPT-4 from 34% to 0.16-4.3% and Silver et al. report about 0.1 with obfuscated names; so much of the base score is surface pattern recall of familiar domains.
agent_test: Test our agent on renamed-predicate variants; the scaffold must hold its score within a few points.

claim: Reasoning models raise Blocksworld sharply (o1-preview 587/600 = 97.8%, Mystery BW 41.6% zero-shot / 52.8% one-shot, randomized 37.3%) but fall to 23.63% on 20-40 step plans (110 instances).
agent_test: Bin test items by plan length; check the scaffold's drop-off point against a plain reasoning run at equal tokens.

claim: Accuracy falls with problem size across independent benchmarks: Natural Plan all models below 5% at 10 cities; Puzzle collapse beyond a complexity threshold; TravelPlanner under 1% for early GPT-4 methods.
agent_test: Plot success against size for scaffold and baseline; look for a shifted cliff, not just higher means.

claim: A sound external verifier that returns the first failing precondition raises accuracy far more than an LLM critic: Blocksworld 40% plain, 55% LLM+LLM, 87-88% LLM+VAL. Caveat: part of the gain is just more samples checked by a sound verifier; blind resampling reached 68-72% (k=15/25) vs 87% with first-error feedback.
agent_test: Compare critic-only vs code-checked precondition/effect simulation on the same instances at equal tokens.

claim: LLM self-verification is unreliable in planning: the LLM verifier passed 38 of 45 invalid plans (84.45% false positives); Natural Plan self-correction lowered accuracy for all models.
agent_test: Measure our own critic's false-pass rate on a labelled set of invalid plans.

claim: Chain of thought helps in planning only when the prompt is tied to the specific problem class: GPT-4 table-to-stack 3.83% zero-shot, 4.98% CoT, 59.3% with stacking-specific prompt, 6.89% with progression-proof prompt; gains do not transfer.
agent_test: Test generic vs task-tailored decomposition prompts; check transfer to a held-out block count.

claim: Letting the LLM translate to PDDL and a classical planner solve gives large gains where the translation is easy: LLM+P 90% on Blocksworld vs 20% LLM-as-planner; but LLM+P fails without an example problem and is weak on several other domains.
agent_test: Give the agent a code tool that holds state and checks applicability; compare with in-head planning.

claim: An LLM can write the successor function and goal test in code, and plain search then solves everything: 502/502 Blocksworld tasks and 1362/1362 Game-of-24 instances in seconds, versus 75% for Tree of Thoughts with about 100 calls each. Caveat: the code was fixed with human-supplied error messages, and passing tests does not prove completeness.
agent_test: Ask the agent to write a small state-transition program for planning-like items; compare accuracy and tokens.

claim: LLM-built PDDL domain models are usually syntactically valid but rarely correct: best model 94% valid PDDL, only 25% heuristically equivalent to the reference; GPT-4 action models needed human correction before Fast Downward reached 95% (Household) and 100% (Logistics).
agent_test: Have the agent write preconditions and effects, then test them on 3 hand-made transitions before trusting them.

claim: A generate-test-reprompt loop with domain critics lifts several planners: LLM-Modulo with up to 10-15 rounds gave BW 82%/Logistics 70% (on 50 previously failed instances each), TravelPlanner 8-25% for GPT-4o and 15% for GPT-4o-mini vs 0-2% direct.
agent_test: Count rounds to success and total tokens; set a round cap and measure marginal gain per round.

claim: Chain-of-thought plus human-readable action tracking of preconditions and effects, learned by instruction tuning with detailed validator feedback, raises Llama-3-8B from 28% to 94% on Blocksworld and 1% to 64% on Mystery BW.
agent_test: Not a scaffold result; use only as evidence that explicit per-step precondition checking is the active ingredient.

claim: Most failures in LLM planning are precondition and state-tracking errors, not goal misunderstanding: ACPBench shows models weakest on action applicability and validation (GPT-4o 52.5% lowest task); direct GPT-4 plans fail on unmet preconditions.
agent_test: Log failure types in our traces; add an applicability-check step and see which error class shrinks.

claim: Generalised-planning programs written by GPT-4 depend strongly on the domain and on debugging: Forest 1.00 and Delivery 0.90 with debugging, Miconic 0.01, Spanner 0.10; no-debug Delivery 0.10; 40% of failures are Python exceptions.
agent_test: Allow a run-and-fix loop for code the agent writes; track the exception share.

claim: Whether reasoning models 'plan' is contested: Shojaee et al. report collapse on larger puzzles, while Opus and Lawsen argue token limits and unsolvable instances confound it, and o1 flags only 27% of unsolvable Blocksworld instances.
agent_test: Add unsolvable items to our test set; score the agent's ability to say 'no plan' correctly.

claim: Human baselines are good but not perfect: 39/50 (78%) valid and 35 of 39 optimal on Blocksworld; LLM assistance did not significantly help (49 vs 48 participants).
agent_test: Use 78% as an anchor only; do not treat it as a ceiling.

claim: Cost of plain long reasoning is high: o1-preview about 40 s and 42 USD per 100 instances vs Fast Downward 0.265 s at 100% on Blocksworld; so token-equal comparisons must count hidden reasoning tokens.
agent_test: Always report tokens including hidden reasoning when comparing arms.

claim: Direct tests of backward (regression) search for LLM planning in STRIPS domains were not found. Indirect evidence from logical reasoning (LAMBADA) favours backward chaining with a modular loop, not backward prose.
agent_test: Run a direct A/B of regression-from-goal vs forward simulation on Blocksworld and Logistics.

claim: Backward chaining with an explicit sub-goal loop beats forward chaining and CoT on proof tasks and uses far fewer model calls (PaLM 540B: +44% relative over CoT on ProofWriter-PUD Depth-5; 11.8x fewer calls than forward Selection-Inference at Depth-5), but plain backward chain-of-thought is not better than forward.
agent_test: Implement O5 as sub-goal decomposition with a per-step check, and A/B it against forward simulation at equal tokens on STRIPS items.

claim: A sound verifier with blind resampling recovers much of a verify-and-reprompt gain: Blocksworld 40% standard, 68% (k=15) and 72% (k=25) resampling, 87% with first-error feedback; Mystery Blocksworld 4% to 14% at best. Self-consistency over 15 samples gave 42%.
agent_test: Report gain per sampled attempt and per token; compare feedback content against plain resampling.

claim: o1-preview rarely detects unsolvable planning goals: 27% flagged on Blocksworld, 16% on randomized Mystery BW, with 54% and 79% returning a full impossible plan and 11.5% of solvable Mystery instances wrongly called impossible. No existence-proof scaffold was tested.
agent_test: Add unsolvable items; let code check reachability.

claim: Reported length cliffs in reasoning models are partly artefacts of output budget, sampling and impossible instances (Blocks World R1 collapse at N=4 at temperature 0 vs N=30 with sampling; River Crossing N>=6 unsolvable; function output restores Hanoi N=15), but collapse at small N (River Crossing N=3) was reported by the authors as real.
agent_test: Sweep plan length with fixed output form, unsolvable items removed, and report the cliff with a range.

claim: LLM-written search code is trusted only after human or validator feedback: Thought of Search needed 1.2-2.4 interactions per function with exact error messages, and no study measured silent-error rates of code that passes its tests.
agent_test: Test any agent-written transition code on an independent hand-made set and a validator before use.

claim: Obfuscation hurts both ways: GPT-4 deceptive names 4.3% and random names 2% on Mystery Blocksworld, so base Blocksworld scores reflect pattern matching, and memorisation versus lost cues is not separated.
agent_test: Rename symbols and change dynamics separately.
